conflicts.point: Whether enterprise AI deployments generate net productivity gains or primarily function as instruments for workforce restructuring and risk shifting.

positions.stance: Automated workflows and algorithmic pipelines demonstrably reduce processing errors and accelerate throughput across logistics and financial operations, yielding net productivity gains.
Reported productivity gains are illusory because they fail to account for the substantial uncompensated verification labor absorbed by front-line service workers.

conflicts.point: Whether regulatory agencies should mandate ex-ante empirical pre-deployment audits for software deployments or rely on runtime telemetry and market competition.

positions.stance: Ex-ante regulatory audits impose prohibitive administrative delays that harm consumers and protect legacy incumbents, making continuous runtime telemetry the superior governance mechanism.
Mandatory pre-deployment safety gating is necessary to prevent structural failures and protect workers from absorbing uncompensated operational risks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether enterprise AI deployments generate net productivity gains or primarily function as instruments for workforce restructuring and risk shifting.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position is stronger because it accounts for the total labor required to maintain system integrity, whereas the accelerationist view measures only automated throughput. Neglecting front-line verification labor produces an incomplete accounting of net productivity at the firm level.

verdicts.conflict: Whether regulatory agencies should mandate ex-ante empirical pre-deployment audits for software deployments or rely on runtime telemetry and market competition.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist position on runtime telemetry is more feasible to implement because mandatory pre-deployment audits create severe administrative backlogs that regulators cannot easily staff or manage. Continuous runtime monitoring aligns better with existing software update cycles and technical oversight capabilities.
